title: Message queues and load leveling

kcs.statement: A message queue stores messages from producers durably until a consumer acknowledges them, so producers and consumers do not need to be up at the same time.

Competing consumers on one queue split its messages between them instead of each getting a copy of every message, but a message that is not acknowledged may be redelivered, possibly to a different consumer.

With queue-based load leveling, when producers enqueue faster than consumers drain, the backlog grows by the rate difference each second and is worked off after the burst ends, keeping consumer load steady.
